title: A lunar rover model, as a beginner
text: A team build for an outreach event on the Chandrayaan-2 mission, organised by NISER's School of Earth and Planetary Sciences: a simple, look-alike model of its rover. It taught me the fundamentals, and gave me the confidence to try something on my own.

title: An FPV drone, a childhood dream
text: On a ₹5,000-a-month scholarship, I planned the whole build first, then saved for months at a time to buy one part. It first flew in 2020, and it has been upgraded ever since.

from.via: the basics, and the confidence to build alone

title: Flying it to new places
text: Once it flew well, it started travelling with me. Filming led to editing: how video files work, codecs, colour, and smoothing out shaky footage.

from.via: a drone that could carry a GoPro

title: An autonomous drone, leading a team
text: The FPV build gave me the confidence to lead a bigger one on club funding: a drone that flies itself, designed as a platform other projects, such as AI vision, can plug into.

title: A 3D printer, my magic pencil
text: After several builds, I knew I needed one. It felt like the magic pencil from Shaka Laka Boom Boom: draw something, and it becomes real. I took it fully apart to repair it, then modded it and moved it to Klipper.

from.via: builds that kept needing custom parts

title: Two Raspberry Pis, then a home server
text: Klipper runs on a tiny Pi Zero 2 W. That Pi got me curious, so a Pi 4B became a home server: a backup drive shared across the house, my phone photos synced to it, my own films and lossless music streamed from it, and our USB printer made wireless.

from.via: Klipper runs on a Raspberry Pi

title: Smart lamps & home automation
text: Printing made these possible: printed trays, towers and diffusers around ARGB LEDs and ESP32 boards running WLED. They dance to music with LedFx, follow the TV as an Ambilight with HyperHDR, and tie into Home Assistant.

title: A phone app, because not everyone has a PC
text: Music-reactive lamps meant LedFx, and LedFx meant a PC running. I couldn't find an open-source phone version, so I wrote one: a native Android app with all of LedFx's effects, streaming to the lamps over Wi-Fi.

from.via: LedFx only ran on a PC

title: A camera, a new way of seeing
text: Then a Canon R10. ISO, shutter and aperture were the easy part. Looking for frames changed how I see: the small, precious details in ordinary places, and how beautiful and varied the world around me is.

title: Pointing it at the sky
text: With a camera and a space-science background, I pointed it up from a plain tripod. My first Orion Nebula was badly trailed, and still looked like a painting. So I went deep.

from.via: a camera, and a space-science background

title: Mosaic Studio, a gift that became an app
text: A mosaic of a friend made from their own photos is a deeply personal gift, but animated ones cost a lot and come in a few fixed styles. So I built my own, first for Windows, then as a free web app that runs anywhere.

from.via: thousands of photos, and a gift idea

title: An astro-tracker, built myself
text: Deep-sky imaging needs a tracking mount, and good ones are expensive. I had some savings, a 3D printer and the skills, so I built my own. This is where the two paths meet.

title: A 3D-printed spectrometer, funded
text: Back at NISER, years of finished builds helped me win funding for an instrument of my own: a mostly 3D-printed visible-to-near-infrared spectrometer for lab scattering studies.

title: A real rover, underwater
text: The same experience got me a position at IIT Bhubaneswar, building hardware for an autonomous rover that inspects oil pipelines up to 100 m deep. It started with a rover model; this one goes to work.

from.via: from a rover model to a working rover

title: A motorized goniometer, for Chandrayaan-2
text: Now the builds feed my research directly: a computer-controlled rig that measures how light scatters off a surface at any angle, for Chandrayaan-2 IIRS photometric correction.

from.via: scattering studies that needed every angle
